conventions.pot_taper: fraction a->w: lin=pos, log=(11**pos-1)/10, revlog=1-(11**(1-pos)-1)/10; halves >= 1 ohm
conventions.ac_sweep: 1 Hz to 200000 Hz, 100 points/decade, transfer v(out)/v(in source)
conventions.f3db: first -3 dB crossings below/above the sweep maximum; null if none inside the sweep
conventions.tran: sine from the DC operating point with 5 ms linear fade-in, max step T/200, settle max(60 ms, 8 cycles), window max(4, round(0.02 f)) cycles
conventions.thd: 100*sqrt(H2^2+...+H15^2)/H1 (Fourier projection of the window minus its mean)
conventions.headroom: largest vin_peak with THD <= 1 %, geometric bisection 5 mV..5 V, 9 steps
conventions.supply_current: sum of DC currents delivered by the *@ supply sources
conventions.opamp_macromodel: RIN; VCCS A0/1Meg into 1Meg||C (pole GBW/A0); gain node clamped to [VEE+VSAT_LO, VCC-VSAT_HI] by a 1000 S softplus clamp (10 mV); unity VCVS + ROUT; IQ from VCC to VEE

circuits.title: Baxandall active bass and treble control
circuits.description: Inverting op-amp with the classic Baxandall feedback network: flat with both knobs at noon, then up to about 15 dB of boost or cut in the lows and highs; listen to how the shelves leave the mids alone.

circuits.title: Common-emitter amplifier with emitter degeneration
circuits.description: Single 2N3904 voltage amplifier, gain about 19x (25 dB) set by Rc over the unbypassed emitter resistor; clean and slightly warm until the collector runs out of swing.

circuits.title: Silicon diode hard clipper
circuits.description: Non-inverting op-amp gain stage (up to 46 dB) into a pair of 1N4148 diodes to ground: buzzy, aggressive distortion that squares off near 0.6 V; listen for the raspy top end and the sustain at high Distortion.

circuits.title: Two-transistor germanium fuzz
circuits.description: The same two-stage feedback fuzz built with leaky AC128 germanium PNPs, wired negative-ground (emitters to +9 V) so it shares a standard supply: rounder and warmer than the silicon version, with a softer clip. With this pair it cleans up less when you roll the guitar volume back (about 18% THD at a quarter turn, against under 5% for the silicon one).

circuits.title: Inductor wah band-pass
circuits.description: Common-emitter stage loaded by a 500 mH inductor tank and buffered by an emitter follower; the Pedal pot bootstraps the tank capacitor so the resonance sweeps from about 480 Hz (heel) to 3 kHz (toe), the vocal "wah". This file is parked mid-sweep.

circuits.title: JFET clean boost
circuits.description: MPF102 common-source stage with partial source bypass: about +15 dB of clean-ish gain with a touch of warm even-order harmonics, then a level knob.

circuits.title: JFET input buffer
circuits.description: J201 source follower with a 1 M input impedance: unity gain, keeps the guitar's treble intact through long cables; it should sound like nothing at all.

circuits.title: MOSFET clean boost
circuits.description: BS170 common-source stage on a gate divider with a partly bypassed source resistor: about +18 dB of clean gain, a touch of even-order warmth when pushed, then a level knob.

circuits.title: Octave-up rectifier fuzz
circuits.description: Gain stage into a transistor phase splitter whose two opposite-phase outputs are full-wave rectified by germanium diodes: the fundamental largely cancels and a ringing octave-up appears, strongest on single notes high on the neck.

circuits.title: Three-knob passive amp tone stack
circuits.description: The classic bass/middle/treble passive network from tube amps, driven from a low-impedance stage into a 1 M grid load: the well-known mid scoop at noon, with Bass, Middle and Treble all interacting.

circuits.title: 9 V power filter with polarity protection and LED
circuits.description: Pedal power entry: a series Schottky blocks a reversed adapter, an RC filter knocks down adapter ripple (VIN models the ripple riding on the 9 V), a red LED shows power and a resistor stands in for the pedal's ~5 mA draw.

circuits.title: RC low-pass filter (1 kHz)
circuits.description: First-order passive low-pass: flat below 1 kHz, then -20 dB/decade; listen for highs being shaved off like a treble roll-off.

circuits.title: Sallen-Key low-pass filter (1 kHz Butterworth)
circuits.description: Second-order unity-gain low-pass on a single 9 V supply: flat to 1 kHz then -40 dB/decade, twice as steep as a plain RC; sounds like a darker, smoother treble cut.

circuits.title: Two-transistor silicon fuzz
circuits.description: Two direct-coupled 2N3904 stages with DC feedback from the second emitter to the first base: thick, sputtery square-wave fuzz with long sustain; the Fuzz knob unbypasses the second emitter.

circuits.title: Op-amp soft-clip overdrive
circuits.description: Non-inverting op-amp with antiparallel diodes in the feedback loop: smooth, compressed overdrive with a mid hump (lows cut below about 720 Hz before clipping) and an active treble tone control; up to about 40 dB of gain.

circuits.title: Germanium treble booster
circuits.description: Single AC128 germanium PNP common-emitter stage (negative-ground wiring) with a small 4.7n input cap: cuts the lows and adds over 30 dB in the upper mids and treble, meant to push an already loud amp into bright, cutting overdrive.

circuits.title: Wien-bridge sine oscillator (1 kHz)
circuits.description: Op-amp Wien bridge on a single 9 V supply: 16k and 10n set about 1 kHz, and two 1N4148 diodes across part of the feedback resistor hold the loop gain at 3 so it settles to a clean sine of about 1.5 V peak (about 1 % THD); a sanity test for transient simulation.
